g.text: C012 · 1D slab modes: TE vs TM

text.style: font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6
font-size: 9.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: The 220 nm Si slab in SiO₂ at 1550 nm guides exactly two modes: TE (n_eff 2.845) and TM (n_eff 2.054) — with very different evanescent tails.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · The cast: the 220 nm slab and its two modes

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: two modes, one law — TE (n_eff 2.845) hugs the core; TM (n_eff 2.054) leaks farther into the cladding (Eq 3.3).

text.style: font-size: 6.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6
